entries.diagnosis: ADDNEQ2's parameter array (MAXPAR, "Maximum number of parameters in combined NEQ", panel ADDNEQ2 3.1) is smaller than the combined normal equation. The "Requested" number is the first request that overflowed, always MAXPAR + 1. It is not how many parameters the solution needs.
entries.remedy: Raise MAXPAR in ADDNEQ2.INP of the option directory used by the failing ADDNEQ2 step (R2S_FIN for the daily final solution). Do not size it from "Requested". Known points: PHREF 2025 (32-41 stations) failed on every day at 1000 and ran all 360 days at 3000. R2S_FIN on gps3 is 6000, matching the 5.2 production panel. Test the busiest day, not an arbitrary one.
entries.source: session log 25.3-25.5 (29 August, 24 failed days); SETTLED.md MAXPAR row; docs/bernese_maxpar_limit.md; reproduced 2026-10-15 on EXAMPLE; AIUB FAQ
entries.confirm: the busiest day of the range completes and writes FIN_*.NQ0

entries.diagnosis: A program's array size, computed from the inputs and options, is more than twice the limit compiled into BSW, so the program stopped. Below twice the limit it only warns ("Unusual big number of parameter").
entries.remedy: Review the options of the failing step, especially whether epoch-wise parameters are pre-eliminated. If the network is simply too large, split it into clusters. Do not raise the compiled limit without asking.
entries.source: AIUB FAQ, "CHKMAX: Dimension for parameter MAXzzz exceeded"

entries.message: OCEAN LOADING CORRECTION VALUES NOT FOUND
entries.diagnosis: Bernese found no readable ocean loading block for STATION NAME in the .BLQ named in FILE NAME. The station can be visibly present and still "not found". Known causes: the block is indented one column left; the block sits after the "$$ END TABLE" line; or the station is missing.
entries.remedy: Run scripts/check_ref_coverage.py --pcf <PCF> --stations <station list>. It reports which case it is. Fix the source file in $D/REF54 named by the PCF's V_BLQINF, not only the campaign's STA copy: R2S_COP copies the campaign's reference files from $D/REF54 at the start of every run.
entries.source: session log 25.2 attempt 4 (PTTN, CALU, URDT); SETTLED.md section 2, BLQ rows
entries.confirm: check_ref_coverage.py exits 0, then the day completes

entries.message: ATMOSPHERIC TIDAL LOADING CORRECTION VALUES NOT FOUND
entries.diagnosis: No atmospheric tidal loading block in the .ATL (FILE NAME) is headed with STATION NAME exactly as the .CRD writes it. Two known causes: the block is headed with the 4-character code only ("PTAG" for "PTAG 22006M005"), or the station is missing. Fiducials are the usual missing ones, because they are what a larger campaign adds.
entries.remedy: Run scripts/check_ref_coverage.py --pcf <PCF> --stations <station list>, fiducials included. Fix the .ATL in $D/REF54 named by V_ATLINF.
entries.source: session log 25.2 attempt 2 (six fiducials missing from PHNAT.ATL); SETTLED.md ATL row (PHDEN DOY 200, PTAG)
entries.confirm: check_ref_coverage.py exits 0, then the day completes

entries.message: ERROR READING ATMOSPHERIC TIDAL LOADING CORRECTION VALUES
entries.diagnosis: The .ATL file is malformed where Bernese reads it. Seen on the last block of a merged file that had no trailing blank line to end it; the same merge had also doubled the carriage returns (CRLF applied twice).
entries.remedy: End the .ATL with a blank line after the last block, and check the line endings (cat -A shows a doubled ^M). Fix the file in $D/REF54.
entries.source: session log 25.2 attempt 3; SETTLED.md seven-reference-types row

entries.diagnosis: The file in FILE NAME does not exist or cannot be read. PGM./SUBR. says which routine wanted it. Seen when a REPR_MODE campaign was started without its STA files. AIUB's FAQ gives the other common case: a missing ${MODEL}/DE421.EPH.
entries.remedy: Check FILE NAME. For campaign STA/ files, the copy step takes them from $D/REF54, which must hold all seven types (.CRD .VEL .ABB .STA .BLQ .ATL .CLU) under the names the PCF variables give. For DE421.EPH, follow README_JPL_EPH.TXT in ${DOC}.
entries.source: reproduction 2026-10-15 (MXP230100, missing EXAMPLE.STA); SETTLED.md seven-reference-types row; AIUB FAQ, "OPNERR: OPEN FAILED"

entries.diagnosis: STATION is in the observations but has no coordinates in the .CRD. AIUB say the usual cause is that RXOBV3 did not rename the station using the .STA, or the RINEX header does not match the .STA's search pattern.
entries.remedy: Add the station to the .CRD (and .STA) under the name the observations use. scripts/check_ref_coverage.py checks that every listed station has a .CRD line.

entries.diagnosis: CCRNXO had no RINEX files to merge for this session. Seen once, and it was a setup fault rather than missing data: sessions 1210-1250 run in parallel in one campaign consumed each other's staged files (SUPERBPE without REPR_MODE; 4 of 5 sessions failed).
entries.remedy: For parallel sessions use REPR_MODE (one campaign per session). Check that the day's RINEX files, fiducials included, are in the directory V_RNXDIR names. If they are and the day really has no data, exclude the day in the plan rather than letting the run find out.

entries.diagnosis: A Helmert transformation had fewer stations than parameters; NUMBER OF STATIONS 0 means no reference station. AIUB give two causes: no station with known ITRF coordinates in the network, or HELMR1's outlier rejection removed them all because one station's coordinate was badly wrong.
entries.remedy: Check the day's reference stations as for HELMR1 NO REDUNDANCY. If they are present, read the HELMR1 output for one station with a large residual, take it out of the datum definition and rerun.
entries.source: AIUB FAQ, "HELMTR: TOO MANY PARAMETERS TO ESTIMATE"

entries.message: NO SUITABLE EPOCHS IN POLE FILE
entries.diagnosis: The pole (ERP) file does not cover the time span the orbit needs. AIUB say this is a wrong pole file, one that is too short, or an unintended processing interval.
entries.remedy: Check that the day's ERP file was fetched (scripts/fetch_igs_products.sh) and covers the day either side of the session.
entries.source: AIUB FAQ, "GETPOL: NO SUITABLE EPOCHS IN POLE FILE"
